language_instruction: **Source language:** Classical (literary) Mongolian in the traditional Uighur-Mongol vertical script, printed from woodblocks (Beijing Kanjur, 1718–20). It is NOT Manchu. Columns run top to bottom and are read from LEFT to RIGHT. Transcribe in Mongolian script (Unicode U+1800 block), one source column per line, in reading order. The margin carries a Chinese section/volume/folio label. Report the primary language in the <language> tag.

The right margin panel carries the Chinese label 諸品經第二卷上二 (Zhu pin jing, volume 2, upper, folio 2). The left margin panel carries a short Mongolian label of about 3–4 words, which I could not read with confidence.</meta>
<margin><unclear>Mongolian margin label of about 3–4 words (section title and folio number), not transcribed</unclear></margin>

At each end is a narrow margin panel with cloud-scroll corner ornaments: the Chinese label is on the right and the Mongolian label is on the left.</image-desc>
<unclear>About 22 columns of Classical Mongolian text in Uighur-Mongol vertical script, read left to right. The text is printed in faded red ink and includes several double-punctuation marks (᠄) at column ends. Not transcribed.</unclear>

<warning>The OCR transcriber reported that the text is printed in faded red ink and the page came as four overlapping strips. The Uighur-Mongol body text could not be read with confidence, so it was not transcribed. This translation therefore carries no body text.</warning>

Collected Sutras <note>original: "諸品經" (Zhu pin jing), the Chinese title used in the Beijing Kanjur for the section of collected dhāraṇī texts, in Tibetan <term>gzungs bsdus</term> <gloss>collected dhāraṇīs</gloss></note>, Volume Two, Upper Part, Folio Two

<margin><unclear>Mongolian margin label of about 3–4 words (section title and folio number), not transcribed</unclear></margin>

<note>A large ornamental border frames the text block with scrolling leaf and cloud motifs. At each end is a narrow margin panel with cloud-scroll ornaments in the corners. The Chinese label sits in the right panel and the Mongolian label in the left.</note>

<unclear>About 22 columns of Classical Mongolian text in Uighur-Mongol vertical script, read left to right. The text is printed in faded red ink and includes several double-punctuation marks (᠄) at column ends. Not transcribed.</unclear>

<summary>This is folio two of the upper part of volume two of the Collected Sutras (Zhu pin jing), the dhāraṇī collection of the red-ink Beijing Mongolian Kanjur woodblock edition. Only the Chinese margin label could be read. The roughly 22 columns of Mongolian text were not transcribed.</summary>
